scope1_onsite_cooling.methodology: Effective IT power (MW) x measured Water Use per Unit of Power (150-1577 gal/MW/day). scope1_onsite_cooling.note: Peak-day demand in Prince William Water's service area runs about 10x the annual average (3060 gal/MW/day observed), so summer stress is far higher than the annual figure implies. A consumptive-use factor of 0.75 applies to the delivered volume.

scope2_electricity.methodology: Effective IT MW x PUE (1.2-1.6, standard vintage) x 24 h/day x 198 gal/MWh (Dominion generation-mix-blended consumption factor) = consumptive water at the generating plant. Per-technology factors are VIRGINIA-SPECIFIC, generation-weighted from USGS plant-level model estimates (2015 release v1.2, July 2024) rather than national medians -- nuclear is 242 gal/MWh here against a national median of 700, because Surry discharges to a tidal estuary and consumes nothing while North Anna evaporates from Lake Anna.
scope2_electricity.note: System-average grid intensity, not marginal-generator attribution -- no published marginal water-intensity dataset exists for PJM/Dominion (NREL Cambium is carbon-only).

Central estimate uses the Prince William Water observed fleet average of 309 gal/MW/day.
scope1_onsite_cooling.note: Peak-day demand in Prince William Water's service area runs about 10x the annual average (3060 gal/MW/day observed), so summer stress is far higher than the annual figure implies. A consumptive-use factor of 0.75 applies to the delivered volume.

scope2_electricity.methodology: Effective IT MW x PUE (1.1-1.5, unknown vintage) x 24 h/day x 198 gal/MWh (Dominion generation-mix-blended consumption factor) = consumptive water at the generating plant. Dominion's 2025 mix is 58% gas / 25% nuclear / 14% renewable / 3% coal. Per-technology factors are VIRGINIA-SPECIFIC, generation-weighted from USGS plant-level model estimates (2015 release v1.2, July 2024) rather than national medians -- nuclear is 242 gal/MWh here against a national median of 700, because Surry discharges to a tidal estuary and consumes nothing while North Anna evaporates from Lake Anna.
scope2_electricity.note: System-average grid intensity, not marginal-generator attribution -- no published marginal water-intensity dataset exists for PJM/Dominion (NREL Cambium is carbon-only).

scope3_embodied.methodology: 5%-15% of the operational (Scope 1 + Scope 2) total, anchored to corporate embodied-vs-operational water disclosure ratios (Privette et al. 2026) -- not a physical estimate specific to this facility's hardware or construction supply chain, which lies entirely outside any Virginia dataset.
scope3_embodied.note: At least one hyperscale operator has disclosed embodied/supply-chain water exceeding 99% of its total corporate water footprint (Privette et al., AGU Advances, 2026) -- that figure reflects a company-wide accounting boundary choice, not a physical per-facility ratio. It is flagged as evidence the 5-15% anchor is a floor, not a ceiling.

scope_water_footprint.total_note: Envelope sum of independent scope minima and maxima -- a conservative bound, not a statistical confidence interval (the three scopes are not assumed to co-vary). The central estimate uses Prince William Water's own observed intensity and is the figure to quote.

benchmark.verdict: Direct on-site estimate (0.023 MGD) sits in the normal measured band for Virginia data centers (JLARC 2024).
